title: A Case of the Mondays: Three Centers Traded, Zero Involving Washington
paragraphs: Well, the Commanders wrapped up their preseason the way you wrap up a garage sale nobody attended: quietly, sadly, and with a 41-3 final score against the Ravens that outgained them 456-177. Baltimore finished its preseason undefeated, which is a sentence that should mean nothing in August and yet still stings like it's Week 17. Dan Quinn made what Riggo's Rag called an "alarming confession" afterward, and honestly at this point I'd pay good money to know what he confessed to, because "we got outgained by 279 yards" is not usually the kind of thing that requires a confession booth.

The bright side, if you squint, is that the real season doesn't count preseason scores, and Adam Peters spent the weekend doing what Adam Peters does: cutting 37 players down to 53 and immediately signaling he's not done. The Commanders somehow ended up with only three cornerbacks on the initial roster, which is the kind of math that works great until literally anyone gets hurt, and wouldn't you know it, top corner Trey Amos is already out for the Week 1 opener against the Eagles. John Keim pointed out that Washington is already down Dorance Armstrong too, with uncertainty around Odafe Oweh, and noted that if they're leaning on heavy zone coverage they'll need the pass rush to bail out the secondary. Cool, cool, no pressure, pass rush.

Meanwhile the center position remains less a competition and more a cry for help. JP Finlay noted he couldn't remember a day with three centers traded around the league and Washington involved in exactly zero of them, which is either admirable restraint or exactly the kind of thing that ages into a Riggo's Rag headline about "unfinished business." Undrafted guard Tanoa Togiai making the roster was the shocker of the weekend per multiple beat writers, proving once again that the most predictable thing about Commanders roster news is that it will not be predictable. Shy Tuttle got released and is expected right back for Week 1, which is the NFL's version of storming out of the house and immediately circling the block.

Quarterback-wise, Sam Hartman's long practice-squad residency in Washington has ended, waived after two years of never actually appearing in a regular season game, while seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis somehow made the initial 53, giving Marcus Mariota a new running mate in the QB room. Add in Trent Scott getting let go with hopes of a practice-squad reunion (the man who caught Jayden Daniels' very first NFL touchdown deserves better treatment than the waiver wire, frankly) and Robert Henry Jr. also getting cut after a strong preseason opener, and you've got a roster that's less finished product and more rough draft with a deadline.

Zooming out to the rest of the league, other 31 teams are going through this same chaotic cut-day theater right now, every fanbase convinced their front office alone has cracked some code, and every front office actually just guessing with better haircuts. It's the most honest week in football: nobody knows anything, everybody has an opinion, and by Wednesday half these rosters will look completely different anyway.

On the actual good news front, UVA throttled NC State 34-8 at Scott Stadium, which is the kind of final score that lets you enjoy a Saturday instead of doom-scrolling through it. The Cavaliers now get Norfolk State next, a get-right game if there ever was one after handling business against an ACC opponent. Elsewhere in the rankings, #14 USC took care of San Jose State 42-26, proving that some teams this weekend actually enjoyed their preseason-adjacent tune-ups instead of getting outgained by nearly 300 yards in prime time.
